new_packages.justification: Torah #243 is a self-contained single-bechina teaching. The Rebbe introduces the concept of the Tzaddik Gadol whose holiness the world cannot bear (line 1), then says 'and this is a bechina of' (וְזֶה בְּחִינוֹת) Shir HaShirim's status as Kodesh Kadashim (line 2), and reinforces it by showing that the paradox of Shir HaShirim (holiest book, no holiness-words) exactly mirrors the paradox of the Tzaddik (holiest person, no visible holiness). This is an independent domain: CONCEALED SUPREME HOLINESS. It is distinct from ordinary wisdom/sekhel packages, prayer packages, or any other common domain. The core principle is: the highest degree of holiness effaces its own outward markers. This principle is applied simultaneously to a person (the Tzaddik) and a text (Shir HaShirim), making them structural equals — genuine bechinot of one another.

observations: Torah #243 has no existing edges in the dataset, so this is a fully new package proposal derived entirely from source text analysis. The teaching is unusually compact — 4 lines — but conceptually precise. The Rebbe makes exactly one explicit bechina equation (the Tzaddik ↔ Shir HaShirim), and this equation is rich enough to support a 4-node package with 4 bechina edges. There is no evil mirror in this Torah: the teaching is wholly about the positive domain of supreme holiness, and the Rebbe does not introduce any negative counterpart. The absence of an evil mirror is consistent with the Torah's aphoristic brevity — it is a single observation about the nature of supreme holiness, not a multi-stage eitza argument with opposing forces. Importantly, Mishlei and Kohelet are mentioned as contrast-concepts (books that DO display holiness-words) but they are not given bechina status — they serve as the foil that reveals Shir HaShirim's uniqueness. They should NOT be added to this package. The recommended data-entry priority is HIGH, as currently the entire Torah #243 domain is a gap in the dataset.
